answer: Anyone can insure an identity against clonehood at a market rate, and when the identity is proved to be a clone the insurer pays out of its own reserve, which turns detection into a revenue stream for whoever performs it. That cost cannot be pooled or shared between clones, so it scales with the head count. Frame it as an echo on the river, collected by the nectar: the farm pays an echo that grows with the size of its cluster, and the nectar is the party that profits from the farm being found out. Because the premium scales with the size of the correlated funding cluster.
